title: Have diabetes, can still eat rice? A safer way to eat it
intro: For most Malaysians, a meal without rice doesn't feel like a meal. If you have diabetes, you don't necessarily have to give up rice. Many people with diabetes still eat rice every day. What matters is how much, what you eat with it, and when you eat. Always follow the advice of your doctor and health officer.

sections.h: Yes, rice is still okay, with the right portion
sections.p: Rice is a carbohydrate, and carbohydrates raise blood sugar. So portion size matters. A simple estimate is one senduk (rice scoop), or about half to three-quarters of a cup. Your doctor or dietitian can help set the right amount for you.

sections.h: The right dishes to pair with it
sections.p: Eat rice with vegetables and protein. For example, rice with ikan bakar, mixed vegetables and soup. This combination makes blood sugar rise more slowly than rice with just gravy. For nasi lemak, roti canai or nasi goreng, have them once in a while and add an egg or vegetables if you can.

sections.h: Type of rice and how it's cooked
sections.p: Brown rice, or rice mixed with brown rice, has more fibre. Many people feel fuller. But portion size still matters. Nasi minyak, nasi beriani and nasi lemak have more oil or santan (coconut milk), so have them less often.

Eating at about the same times every day can help keep your sugar readings more stable. This is even more important if you take medicine or insulin. Don't skip meals without discussing with your doctor, because your sugar can drop too low.

Walking after meals, chair exercises and wall push-ups are good, joint-friendly options. Wear comfortable shoes and check your feet after walking. If you take insulin or certain medicines, bring some sweets or a sweet drink just in case.

action: Use the same senduk every day and take about one scoop of rice.
Make sure every plate of rice has vegetables and one protein dish.
Cut rice cooked with santan or lots of oil down to once in a while only.
Walk 10 minutes after meals if your doctor allows.
Write down your sugar readings and what you eat in a small notebook, and show it to your doctor.
doctor: See your doctor first before making big changes to how much rice you eat, doing puasa sunat (optional fasting), or starting exercise, especially if you take insulin or medicine that can lower your sugar too much. Get urgent treatment if you feel shaky, have cold sweats, feel confused or dizzy, or if your sugar is very high together with vomiting or feeling very weak. Also see your doctor if you have a wound on your foot that won't heal. Don't change or stop your medicine on your own. Discuss with your doctor.

faq.q: If I stop eating rice completely, can I take less medicine?
faq.a: Don't make this decision on your own. Suddenly cutting out rice while on medicine can make your sugar drop too low. Talk to your doctor before making big changes, and let your doctor decide about your medicine.

faq.q: Is white bread or noodles better than rice?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Bread, noodles, bihun and rice are all carbohydrates. What matters is the portion size and what you eat with it.

faq.q: Is it true that cooled rice raises blood sugar less?
faq.a: Some studies show a small effect, but it differs from person to person. It's not a replacement for measuring your rice. If you want to try it, monitor your sugar readings and share them with your doctor.
